Hidden character highlight playground

A development-only page for looking at how the extension draws the markers. It links the real extension/content/hidden-character-marks.css and repeats the exact markup the detector builds, so what you see here is what a real page shows. Every hidden character in the text below is a numeric reference; nothing invisible is stored in this file. The page has no script of any kind.

The marker palette is chosen from prefers-color-scheme, which follows the browser or the operating system, not the page. To see the dark palette while this page is otherwise light, open DevTools → ⋮ → More tools → Rendering and set Emulate CSS prefers-color-scheme to dark.

Markers and severities

The colour encodes how suspicious the character is: red for characters that are never needed in prose, amber for ones that also appear legitimately (emoji, Persian, Indic), blue for look-alike spaces. Each marker spells out the code point it replaced, such as U+200B, in a monospace face so the hex digits line up between markers. Hover a marker for the kind of character it is.

invisible U+E0001 · often legitimate U+200D · space variant U+00A0

This is the markup createMarkElement() produces. In the page the hidden character is replaced by the marker rather than sitting next to it, so the marker reads as the character's code point exactly where the character used to be.

<span class="ii-hidden-character ii-hidden-character--hidden" data-ii-character="󠀁" title="Unicode tag characters" role="img" aria-label="Hidden character U+E0001">U+E0001</span>

1. Baseline: light page, light palette

The ordinary case. Dark red, amber and blue text on their 14–16% tints over white. All three should be comfortably readable.

#ffffff · #1f2024

The gap counts as U+200B fully successful, and the flag is a U+FE0F selector that is also used by emoji, so it stays amber. The metric never leaves U+2009 the error budget.

2. Baseline: dark page, light palette (the reported problem)

This is the case from the screenshot. The panel is a dark chat bubble, but the marker colours come from the light palette, because prefers-color-scheme is still light: the dark red #b3261e and the 14% red wash sit on a near-black background. If this section is hard to read, that is the bug, and the dark block at the end of the stylesheet is what would fix it once the palette follows the page instead of the browser.

#1b1c1f · #e8eaed
  • Datadog: U+E0001 You can configure the monitor to Evaluate as zero, forcing the metric to zero and failing the SLI threshold. U+E0002
  • Prometheus/Grafana: Time series naturally disappear when missing. You append or vector(0) to the PromQL query to force the calculation to fail.
  • Assume Good (Fail-Open / Skip)
    This treats the gap as 100% successful or omits the time window entirely so the error budget does not burn.
  • Datadog: U+200D Configured using the Show OK setting. U+00A0

3. Neutral surfaces

Grey pages from white to mid grey, including one panel whose own text is already low contrast. On the mid-grey and low-contrast panels the marker has to stay legible without the text or the wash disappearing.

#f6f7f9 · raised

A thin U+2009 space inside a code sample.

#dcdfe4 · grey

A zero-width U+200B separator between two words.

#9aa0a6 · mid grey

A soft U+00AD hyphen at the end of a line.

#d9dbdf on #a8acb2 · already low contrast

Deliberately washed-out text with a U+2060 word joiner in it.

4. Saturated panels where the marker colour collides with the background

Callouts, banners and code blocks are often painted in exactly the red, amber or blue the marker uses. On the red panel a red marker should vanish; on the blue panel a blue one should. These are the cases a prefers-color-scheme palette cannot see.

#1a5fb4 · same as the spacing colour

Blue panel with a U+00A0 space variant and a U+200B zero-width space.

#b3261e · same as the hidden colour

Red panel with an U+E0001 invisible marker and an U+FE0F amber one.

#8a5a00 · same as the ambiguous colour

Amber panel with an U+200D ambiguous marker.

#1e6b3a · green

Green panel with a U+2060 word joiner.

#5b2a86 · purple

Purple panel with an U+3000 ideographic space.

5. Gradients and split backgrounds

No single background colour to test against: the same paragraph runs from near-black to white, and a marker can straddle the boundary. A palette picked from prefers-color-scheme has to be readable at both ends.

dark → light

A zero-width U+200B space on the dark end and a thin U+2009 space on the light end.

multi-hue

A tag payload U+E0001 over blue, purple and amber.

hard half/half split

Dark side U+E0002 and light side, in one line.

6. Patterned and photographic backgrounds

An inline SVG stripe pattern and a busy multi-stop background: a translucent wash disappears against texture, and the label and its colour have to carry the meaning on their own.

svg stripe pattern

A word joiner U+2060 over diagonal stripes.

busy multi-stop

A soft hyphen U+00AD over a patchy background.

7. Translucency, opacity and filters

Anything that changes how the text is composited changes the contrast the marker actually achieves: a backdrop-filter card, a parent with opacity, and a parent with a CSS filter all do it.

glass card, backdrop-filter

A tag payload U+E0001 behind frosted glass.

parent opacity: 0.55

A mid-sentence U+200B zero-width space.

parent filter: grayscale(0.7) contrast(1.3)

A thin U+2009 space behind a filter.

8. Inherited text properties

The marker sets its own font family and size but everything else is inherited, so a page that stretches, spaces or decorates its text stretches the marker too.

serif, letter-spacing 0.28em, word-spacing 0.6em

A tag U+E0001 payload in spaced serif text.

uppercase + small-caps

A zero-width U+200B space in shouting text.

wavy underline

A decorat U+00AD ed word with a wavy underline.

direction: rtl

RTL text U+202E with a bidi override in it.

white-space: nowrap, scrolls sideways

One long unbroken line U+2060 that cannot wrap at all, so it overflows instead.

writing-mode: vertical-rl

Vertical U+3000 text

10. Density and adjacency

A marker replaces a zero-width character, so several of them can end up touching each other with no space between, or filling a line on their own.

U+200B

A paragraph that contains nothing but one marker.

Three back to back:U+200BU+200BU+200Bthen words again.

A long run of adjacent markers, to check that they wrap as a group and never overlap.

U+E0001U+200DU+00A0U+E0001U+200DU+00A0U+E0001U+200DU+00A0U+E0001U+200DU+00A0

A marker at the start of a line U+200B and one at the end of the same line U+2009

Between punctuation: (U+2060), [U+00AD] and after bold textU+200B.

11. Type size and line height

The marker is 0.8em with a monospace label, so it scales with the text. At line-height: 1 it is taller than the line box; at 40px the label and the wash have much more area to look at.

40px

zoom / transform: scale()

12. The active highlight (Show / Prev / Next)

The marker the popup last jumped to gets ii-hidden-character--active, drawn as a currentColor ring plus a pulse. The ring should follow each severity's own colour. The pulse shadow is currently hard-coded red, so watch the amber and blue markers in the row.

U+E0001 U+200D U+00A0

The same three on a dark page, where the ring and the pulse have to be visible against near-black.

U+200B U+00AD U+2009

13. Before and after Show

The first paragraph holds the real hidden characters, so it looks like ordinary prose. The second is the same text after Show: each hidden character became a marker. The two should have the same length and line breaks.

14. Right-to-left text

In RTL text the marker is laid out from the right, and a bidirectional control marker sits in a paragraph whose direction it changes.

dir="rtl"

هذا نص عربي U+200F يحتوي على علامة.

Mixed English and العربية with a U+2066 isolate marker.

15. Narrow columns and unbreakable tokens

The marker is inline-block, so it is an atomic box: in a very narrow column it must not be split, and inside a token that is allowed to break anywhere it must not be lost.

12ch wide

Very narrow text with a U+E0001 marker in it.

overflow-wrap: anywhere

averylongunbroken U+2009 token

12ch wide on dark

Narrow and dark with a U+200D marker.

16. How to look at the other palettes

  1. Dark palette: DevTools → ⋮ → More tools → Rendering → Emulate CSS prefers-color-scheme → dark. Every section above re-renders with the dark block of the stylesheet; sections 2, 6, 7 and 12 are the interesting ones.
  2. Light palette on a dark page is sections 2 and 4 with emulation left on light: the reported bug in one screen.
  3. Forced colours (Windows high contrast): same Rendering menu → Emulate forced-colors: active. The stylesheet has no forced-colors block, so the wash and the ring may drop out entirely.
  4. Colour blindness: Rendering menu → Emulate vision deficiencies. Red, amber and blue are the classic ambiguous set, so check deuteranopia and tritanopia.
  5. Print and PDF: Ctrl/Cmd + P. Backgrounds are usually dropped, leaving only the label and its colour.
  6. Zoom: 50% and 200% browser zoom, and a 320px wide window, to check the marker in a phone-width column.
